ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, on a smooth horizontal plane, two nails A and B are fixed. One end of a long thin rope is tied to a small ball, and the other end is fixed to nail A. At the beginning, the small ball and nails A and B are all on one straight line (the position shown in the figure), and a large part of the thin rope is wound around the two nails in the clockwise direction as viewed from above. Now the small ball is made to undergo circular motion on the horizontal plane with initial velocity v0 in the counterclockwise direction as viewed from above, so that the rope wound between the two nails is gradually released. After the rope is completely released, compared with before the release, which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The tension of the thin rope on the small ball becomes smaller

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The tension of the thin rope on the small ball becomes smaller
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the small ball is located on the left side, and nails A and B are located on the right side, with A to the left of B; the small ball and A, B are roughly on the same horizontal line. The thin rope extends from the small ball to the right to the nail area, and between the two nails A and B it appears as multiple horizontal rope segments, indicating that the rope is wound multiple times between the two nails. Reasoning: Before release, because a relatively large part of the rope is wound between A and B, the effective rope length corresponding to the small ball's actual circular motion is shorter, that is, the radius of the circular motion is smaller. The problem states that the small ball moves in the counterclockwise direction as viewed from above, and the wound rope segments are gradually released; when the rope is completely released, the rope length originally wound between the two nails is all transformed into free rope length, and one end of the rope is fixed at A, so the final radius of the small ball's motion around the fixed end A is larger than before release. The horizontal plane is smooth; gravity and the supporting force do no horizontal work in the vertical direction, and the tension of the rope provides centripetal force in the circular motion and does not change the speed, so the speed remains v0. From the centripetal force formula T = m v0^2 / r, it can be known that v0 is unchanged and the radius r after release becomes larger, so the tension of the thin rope on the small ball becomes smaller.
